market.question: Will Trump talk to Emmanuel Macron in January?
market.rules_text:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual talks with Donald Trump between January 1 and January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

A talk is defined as any interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

data_availability.evidence_clause: The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.
data_availability.rationale: Phone calls and video calls between heads of state are often not publicly disclosed or are reported only after significant delay; a call could occur within the window but not be reported until after resolution, or never be confirmed publicly at all.

definitional_gaps.evidence_clause: A talk is defined as any interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.
definitional_gaps.rationale: The definition is reasonably broad but excludes written communication (texts, letters); edge cases like a brief exchange at a multilateral summit or a third-party-mediated call could be disputed as to whether they qualify as a direct 'verbal communication'.

all_runs.failure_scenario: A phone call between Trump and Macron occurs but is only reported by a single French outlet and denied by the White House, leaving the resolver unable to establish a 'consensus of credible reporting' and forcing a disputed or arbitrary resolution.
all_runs.load_bearing_clause: "The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting."

resolver_discretion.evidence_clause: The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.
resolver_discretion.rationale: The resolver must independently judge which outlets are 'credible,' how many reports constitute a 'consensus,' and whether a reported interaction meets the definition of a 'talk' — all of which are subjective judgment calls with no mechanical check.

source_ambiguity.evidence_clause: The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.
source_ambiguity.rationale: No specific outlets or sources are named; 'credible reporting' and 'consensus' are inherently subjective and leave the resolver to decide which reports qualify and how many constitute a consensus.

timing_edge_cases.evidence_clause: This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual talks with Donald Trump between January 1 and January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.
timing_edge_cases.rationale: The end_date_utc is listed as 2026-01-31T00:00:00+00:00 (midnight UTC), which is actually January 30 at 7 PM ET, conflicting with the rules text's stated cutoff of January 31, 11:59 PM ET — this timezone/timestamp mismatch creates a genuine timing edge case.
